title: Review panel removed from the UAP Disclosure Act

tellings.quote: Uh, I think that was my biggest disappointment that that was removed from the first version of the UAP Disclosure Act
(a) Establishment.--There is established as an independent agency a board to be known as the ``Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board''.

(1) In general.--The President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, shall appoint, without regard to political affiliation, 9 citizens of the United States to serve as members of the Review Board to ensure and facilitate the review, transmission to the Archivist, and public disclosure of government records relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena.

plain: The first version of the UAP Disclosure Act set up an independent board to release government files on UFOs, and that board was later cut. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's current term for UFOs, and the act was an amendment to the yearly defense bill, put forward in the Senate by Chuck Schumer and Mike Rounds on 13 July 2023. Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, tells Michels that losing the board was his biggest disappointment. The bill's own text shows what was lost: it says that 'there is established as an independent agency a board to be known as the "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board"', with nine citizens appointed by the President with the Senate's consent 'to ensure and facilitate the review, transmission to the Archivist, and public disclosure' of UAP records. Graves gives the removal itself from his own knowledge; the quoted text is the version as first written.
